# pstack in T3 Code

pstack skills use Cursor names. In T3 Code, read this file once per session, then map each Cursor name in a skill with the tables below. `<skills>` means the folder that holds `poteto-mode/` and this file's folder, usually `~/.agents/skills/` or a project's `.agents/skills/`. If a Cursor field has no row, drop it and say so. Never pass a field or value the tool schema rejects.

T3 Code runs many providers. These rows hold in every T3 thread, whichever provider runs it. Spawn pstack subagents with the T3 tools below, not a provider's own subagent tool, so per-role models and cross-provider panels work and every child shows in the T3 app.

## Tools

| Cursor | T3 Code |
| --- | --- |
| `Task` | `delegate_task`. The child sees only the `task` text, never this conversation, so every brief stands alone: goal, scope, file paths, done check, and what to report. |
| `subagent_type` | Drop it. Set `role` instead: `implementation` for code, `review` for reviewers, `research` for read-only investigators, `general` otherwise. See Subagent fields for named agents. |
| `AskQuestion` | `AskUserQuestion` when the session offers it. Otherwise ask in plain text and end the turn. To answer a question another thread is waiting on, use `t3_pending_request_list`, `t3_pending_request_read`, and `t3_pending_request_respond`. |
| Open a todolist | Use the session's todo or plan tool if it has one. Otherwise keep the list in your reply and update it at each phase. |
| Run another pstack skill (`/name` or "the **name** skill") | `Read` `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md` and follow it. When you tell the user to type it, write `/<name>`. |
| `Grep`, `Glob` | The session's search tools, or `rg` in the shell. |

## Subagent fields

| Cursor | T3 Code |
| --- | --- |
| `subagent_type: generalPurpose` | A plain `delegate_task`. |
| `poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko` | A `delegate_task` whose `task` starts with the body of `<skills>/pstack-t3/agents/poteto-agent.md` or `<skills>/pstack-t3/agents/comment-sicko.md`, then the absolute path of this file with "read it first", then the brief. For `poteto-agent`, the brief also carries the absolute path of `<skills>/poteto-mode/SKILL.md`. |
| `readonly: true` | `role: "research"` or `"review"`, and the brief says "do not edit files and run no git command that writes". T3 has no read-only switch, so check `git status` afterward. |
| `readonly: false` | Omit. Children keep the thread's MCP servers. |
| `environment: "cloud"` | `isolation: "worktree"`. The child gets its own checkout of this thread's current local commit, after project setup. Uncommitted edits are not copied, so commit or name what it needs. |
| `environment: "local"` | Omit, or `isolation: "shared"`. Only one writer per checkout. |
| `cloud_base_branch: <b>` | `isolation: "worktree"`, and tell the worker to check out `<b>` first. |
| `run_in_background: true`, `is_background` | `mode: "async"`, the default. The child's completion wakes this thread, so end the turn instead of polling. Use `task_status` only when you need a result mid-turn, and `task_cancel` to stop one. |
| `resume` | Spawn a fresh `delegate_task` with the original brief, every later directive, and the earlier result pasted in. Do not send new work to a child's `childThreadId`. |
| `file_attachments` | List the paths in the brief. |

A named worker that needs its own top-level thread, worktree, and branch, such as a PR owner the operator will open later, is a `t3_thread_launch` with `workspaceStrategy` `{"type":"worktree","baseRef":"<parent>","branch":"<branch>","startFromOrigin":false}`. Keep its `threadId` and follow it with `t3_thread_read` or `t3_thread_wait`. Use it only where the playbook gives a worker its own branch to own, not for ordinary fan-out.

## Models

pstack names models by slug. T3 names them by provider instance, model id, and options, all listed by `orchestrator_capabilities`. Call it once before the first spawn.

| Cursor | T3 Code |
| --- | --- |
| `claude-<family>-<version>-<effort>[-fast]`, such as `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` | `target: {"providerInstanceId": "<the Claude instance>", "model": "claude-opus-5-5", "options": {"<its reasoning option id>": "xhigh"}}`. `-fast` sets the model's fast option, such as `fastMode: true`, when it has one. |
| `grok-*`, `cursor-grok-*`, `composer-*`, such as `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` | The Grok instance when `orchestrator_capabilities` says it can run child tasks. Otherwise the configured role line. With no line, use the strongest code model from a provider other than the judgment role's, so a two-family panel stays two-family, and say which you chose. |
| `gpt-*`, such as `gpt-5.6-sol-max` | The Codex instance with that model id and its reasoning option set to the effort token. `-fast` sets its fast service tier when it has one. |
| `inherit-parent` or `auto` | Omit `target`, so the child runs on this thread's model. |
| The `pstack-models.mdc` rule, `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` | `~/.agents/pstack-models.md`. No provider loads it on its own, so read it with this file. If the file or the role's line is missing, use the skill's default slug, mapped with the rows above. |
| A role value `<instance>/<model> <effort>[ fast]`, such as `claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 xhigh` | `target: {"providerInstanceId": "<instance>", "model": "<model>", "options": {...}}` with the effort on the model's reasoning option and `fast` on its fast option. |

The reasoning option's id differs by provider, such as `effort` or `reasoningEffort`. Read it from the model's `options` in `orchestrator_capabilities`. pstack's ladder is `max` > `xhigh` > `high` > `medium` > `low`. Never pick a value above `max`, such as `ultra` or `ultrathink`, unless the role line names it. If `delegate_task` rejects an adjusted target, use the role's line or default and say so.

## setup-pstack

Follow its steps with these changes:

- Detect. The detected models are the models of every provider in `orchestrator_capabilities` whose `canRunChildTask` is true, each with the values of its reasoning option. Write a real model as `<instance>/<model> <effort>`, such as `codex/gpt-6.1-sol xhigh`. The effort is the last token, or the one before a trailing `fast`, so the budget step works as written.
- Defaults. Map each default slug with the rows above. A Grok default with no usable Grok instance becomes the strongest detected code model from another provider than the `judgment and prose` default. Mark it as needing a choice in step 3c.
- Write. Write `~/.agents/pstack-models.md` with no frontmatter, then the comment lines, the `# budget` line, and one line per role from step 5. Overwrite the whole file. Never put the role lines in `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`. Tell the user it applies to every new T3 thread.

## Paths

| Cursor | T3 Code |
| --- | --- |
| `.cursor/skills/`, `~/.cursor/skills/` | `.agents/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/` |
| `~/.cursor/plugins/`, `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` | `<skills>`. pstack's version is in `<skills>/pstack-t3/pstack.json`. |
| `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, always-applied rules | The repo's `AGENTS.md`, or `CLAUDE.md` when the repo keeps its rules there. The model rule is the exception. See Models. |
| `.cursor/worktrees/` | The worktrees T3 lists with `t3_worktree_list`. `t3_worktree_status` reads one. |
| The current agent's store (path in the system prompt) | `~/.agents/pstack-store/<repo-slug>/`. Create it. |
| `https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/<path>` | The local copy when this tree ships it: `<skills>/<name>/` for skills, `<skills>/pstack-t3/guide/` for `docs/guide/`, `<skills>/pstack-t3/README.md`, `<skills>/pstack-t3/agents/`. Read it and never fetch it. Give the user the URL when they need a link. |
| Transcripts in `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/` | T3 threads. Find them with `t3_thread_search` or `t3_thread_list`. Read one with `t3_thread_read`, `view: "messages"` for the conversation or `"activity"` for tool calls. A delegated child's transcript is its `childThreadId`. A thread's last activity, not a file mtime, says whether it is live. |

## Waking and scheduling

| Cursor | T3 Code |
| --- | --- |
| `/loop` (Cursor's built-in wake mechanism) | Pick the T3 wake for what you wait on. A PR event (checks finish or fail, a new comment or review, a conflict) is `watch_pull_request`. Handle the existing comments, arm it, and end the turn. Another event is an async `delegate_task` watcher, a small script that blocks until the event, whose completion wakes you. A heartbeat is `schedule_task` with `{"type":"interval","everyMs":<ms>}` and the tick prompt, bound to this thread. `/loop until X` puts the predicate in the tick prompt, and the tick that sees it met calls `delete_scheduled_task`. |
| `/loop 1h` | `schedule_task` with `{"type":"interval","everyMs":3600000}`. Keep the literal text `/loop 1h` where a plan or status message names it, because `poteto-mode/scripts/check-plan.mjs` checks for it, and record the scheduled task's id beside it. |
| Cursor Automations: routines, `update_state` routine calls, `api2.cursor.sh/automations` webhooks, routine wakes | `schedule_task`. A timed routine is `{"type":"interval",...}` or `{"type":"fixed_time","timeOfDay":"09:00","weekdays":[1,2,3,4,5]}`. A webhook routine is `{"type":"webhook"}`, and its result's `webhookUrl` is the URL. If `webhookUrl` is absent, tell the user to enable T3 Connect remote access. The run sees the request only through `{{body.<field>}}`, `{{headers.<name>}}`, `{{body}}`, or `{{request}}` placeholders in the prompt, so name each field the sender posts there. Set `bindToCurrentThread: false` only when the user wants a fresh thread per run. |
| `SendToUser` secret requests, sender keys | `request_secret`. You never see the value. Pass the returned `secretRef` once, such as to a webhook's `signature`: `{"header":"<header>","encoding":"hex","prefix":"sha256=","secretRef":"<ref>"}`. A sender that cannot sign a body relies on the unguessable URL. Say so, and send no `Authorization` or `X-Automation-Key` header. |

## Cursor-only features

When a step needs a feature with no row, put one line in your reply, `Skipped in T3 Code: <step>. <reason>.`, then go on to the next step. Do not stop, ask, or retry. When a later step needs what the skipped step made, such as a URL or a key, leave a placeholder and name it in the line.

| Cursor | T3 Code |
| --- | --- |
| Bugbot | Bugbot comments on a GitHub PR are ordinary review threads, so triage them with the forge command that the step gives. Skip a step that starts, waits for, or configures Bugbot when the PR has no Bugbot check or comment. |
| Cursor cloud agent, cloud VM, its status in the Cursor dashboard | A `delegate_task` with `isolation: "worktree"`, as in Subagent fields. Its status is `task_status`. Its log is `t3_thread_read` on its `childThreadId`. Skip a step that needs the cloud machine itself. |
| A built-in PR tool | The forge command that the step gives, such as `gh pr create`. Then call `link_pull_request` for every PR you open or take over, each layer of a stack included. A PR you wait on is `watch_pull_request` from the thread that owns it. A delegated child cannot watch, so a child that owns a PR uses the step's `scripts/watch-pr` and returns, and its parent watches. Call `unwatch_pull_request` before you hand work back. |
| `control-ui`, `control-cli` from `cursor-team-kit` | Browser and web UIs: `preview_open`, `preview_navigate`, `preview_snapshot`, `preview_click`, `preview_type`, `preview_press`, `preview_wait_for`, `preview_resize`, and `preview_recording_start` / `preview_recording_stop` for video. iOS and Android simulators: `device_list`, `device_open`, `device_screenshot`, `device_close`. CLIs and TUIs: drive them from the shell, and capture the output as evidence. An Electron app with no preview path is a skip. |
| Other `cursor-team-kit` skills, such as `/deslop` | Follow `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md` when it exists. Otherwise skip with the line. |
| `create-skill` (Cursor's built-in for authoring SKILL.md files) | The session's own skill-authoring skill when it has one. Otherwise follow the step's own rules and pstack's Authoring a skill playbook alone. |
| Custom Modes, Option+Enter, the Agents Window, Plan Mode | T3 has no mode toggle. Start each new task with `/poteto-mode`. T3's plan interaction mode can stand in for Plan Mode. |
| Cursor's built-in babysit skill, or any other Cursor built-in a step warns you away from | Nothing to avoid. Follow the pstack step. |

## Any other Cursor name

Map a Cursor name with no row to its T3 meaning when one is plain. A Cursor restart is a T3 Code restart: local children stop, while scheduled tasks, linked PRs, and pushed branches survive. "The Cursor environment's MCPs" are the MCP tools this session lists. Otherwise skip with the line.
